categories.main_business_segments: Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) operates primarily in three segments: Maintenance of Airplanes and Vehicles, Engines, and Industrial Technology Services. The military business includes manufacturing, maintenance, and upgrades of domestic military aircraft and engines. The civil aviation business involves design and OEM production of airframe structures and engine parts for international commercial aircraft. Industrial technology services focus on energy systems, aviation services, information services, and related aerospace technology applications.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: AIDC employs advanced aerospace manufacturing technologies including hot forging for military aircraft engine structures, metal forming CAE research, robotic assembly systems, high-efficiency CNC machining, and composite material manufacturing such as thermoplastic composites. The company also develops intelligent manufacturing systems integrating AI and lean production methods. Maintenance technologies include building repair capabilities and developing parts with commercial sources. Energy management systems and gas turbine generator technologies are also key development areas.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include the Republic of China Ministry of National Defense and National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology for military products. Major international aerospace manufacturers such as Boeing, Airbus, Bombardier, GE Aviation, Rolls-Royce, Honeywell, Pratt & Whitney, and Lockheed Martin are primary customers for civil aviation products. Industrial technology services are provided to domestic enterprises including Taiwan Power Company, CPC Corporation, and various private sector clients, as well as some foreign entities.
categories.geographic_coverage: AIDC operates mainly in Taiwan with manufacturing complexes in Taichung, Shalu, and Gangshan. It has a US subsidiary (AIDC USA LLC) based in Arizona to support project management and trading services. Its civil aviation customers are located globally, including Europe, the United States, and Japan. The company’s industrial technology services also extend to domestic and some international clients.
categories.supply_chain_position: AIDC functions primarily as a Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier in the aerospace supply chain, providing aircraft structural parts, engine sub-assemblies, and components. It is involved in design, manufacturing, assembly, testing, and maintenance, positioning itself upstream and midstream in the aerospace industry supply chain. It also manages outsourcing to suppliers for parts and components, integrating the domestic aerospace supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include advancing military aircraft programs such as the advanced jet trainer and F-16 upgrades, developing new basic jet trainers, and expanding drone production capabilities. In civil aviation, focus is on securing orders, developing composite materials, and entering aircraft engine maintenance (MRO). Industrial technology R&D targets energy management systems, renewable energy, and aviation services for disaster prevention. The company invests 2-4% of revenue annually in R&D, emphasizing AI integration, lean manufacturing, and composite technology development.
categories.revenue_model: AIDC generates revenue primarily through product sales and service contracts, including manufacturing and maintenance of military and commercial aircraft and engines. Revenue is also derived from industrial technology services such as energy storage system installations and aviation-related technical services. The company recognizes revenue based on progress of performance obligations, with contract assets and liabilities managed accordingly.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In the defense sector, AIDC leverages its experience from indigenous fighter and trainer programs to maintain a competitive edge in maintenance and upgrades, supported by government defense budgets. In civil aviation, it competes as a strategic partner and Tier 1 supplier to major global aerospace firms, facing competition from emerging low-cost clusters and established global suppliers. The company leads Taiwan’s aerospace industry and is part of the Taiwan A-Team 4.0 Alliance to strengthen supply chain competitiveness. In industrial technology services, it occupies niche markets leveraging aerospace technology.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: AIDC reported consolidated operating revenue of NT$30.24 billion in 2022, a 27.4% increase from the previous year, with net profit after tax of NT$1.62 billion and earnings per share of NT$1.73. The company has total assets of approximately NT$42.7 billion and equity of NT$15.8 billion as of 2022. It has shown significant profitability growth driven by military deliveries, civil aviation recovery, and energy services expansion. The company maintains a stable financial structure with a debt ratio around 63% and invests steadily in R&D.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: AIDC emphasizes its integrated capabilities in design, manufacturing, maintenance, and repair of military and commercial aerospace products, supported by advanced technologies and quality certifications from global aerospace leaders. Its unique value lies in combining military-grade aerospace expertise with civil aviation manufacturing, enabling technology transfer and supply chain integration in Taiwan. The company’s commitment to sustainability, energy transition technologies, and local repair capabilities further differentiate it as a resilient and innovative aerospace leader.
